FILE: WildsEngine.Core\Processing\Base\StateInstructionBase.cs
############################################################
    1: using System;
    2: using System.Collections.Generic;
    3: using WildsEngine.Core.Abstractions;
    4: 
    5: namespace WildsEngine.Core.Processing
    6: {
    7:     public abstract class StateInstructionBase :
    8:         IStateInstruction
    9:     {
   10:         private readonly Dictionary<string, object?> _arguments;
   11:         private readonly Dictionary<string, object?> _metadata;
   12: 
   13:         protected StateInstructionBase(
   14:             string intent,
   15:             object? payload = null,
   16:             IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, object?>>? arguments = null,
   17:             IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, object?>>? metadata = null)
   18:         {
   19:             if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(intent))
   20:             {
   21:                 throw new ArgumentException(
   22:                     "Instruction intent cannot be empty.",
   23:                     nameof(intent));
   24:             }
   25: 
   26:             Id = Guid.NewGuid();
   27:             Intent = intent;
   28:             Payload = payload;
   29: 
   30:             _arguments = CreateDictionary(arguments);
   31:             _metadata = CreateDictionary(metadata);
   32:         }
   33: 
   34:         public Guid Id { get; }
   35: 
   36:         public string Intent { get; }
   37: 
   38:         public object? Payload { get; }
   39: 
   40:         public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?> Arguments =>
   41:             _arguments;
   42: 
   43:         public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?> Metadata =>
   44:             _metadata;
   45: 
   46:         protected void SetArgument(
   47:             string key,
   48:             object? value)
   49:         {
   50:             ValidateKey(key, nameof(key));
   51: 
   52:             _arguments[key] = value;
   53:         }
   54: 
   55:         protected void SetMetadata(
   56:             string key,
   57:             object? value)
   58:         {
   59:             ValidateKey(key, nameof(key));
   60: 
   61:             _metadata[key] = value;
   62:         }
   63: 
   64:         protected bool RemoveArgument(string key)
   65:         {
   66:             ValidateKey(key, nameof(key));
   67: 
   68:             return _arguments.Remove(key);
   69:         }
   70: 
   71:         protected bool RemoveMetadata(string key)
   72:         {
   73:             ValidateKey(key, nameof(key));
   74: 
   75:             return _metadata.Remove(key);
   76:         }
   77: 
   78:         private static Dictionary<string, object?> CreateDictionary(
   79:             IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, object?>>? source)
   80:         {
   81:             var result =
   82:                 new Dictionary<string, object?>();
   83: 
   84:             if (source == null)
   85:             {
   86:                 return result;
   87:             }
   88: 
   89:             foreach (var pair in source)
   90:             {
   91:                 ValidateKey(pair.Key, nameof(source));
   92: 
   93:                 result[pair.Key] = pair.Value;
   94:             }
   95: 
   96:             return result;
   97:         }
   98: 
   99:         private static void ValidateKey(
  100:             string key,
  101:             string parameterName)
  102:         {
  103:             if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(key))
  104:             {
  105:                 throw new ArgumentException(
  106:                     "Instruction keys cannot be empty.",
  107:                     parameterName);
  108:             }
  109:         }
  110:     }
  111: }

############################################################
FILE: WildsEngine.Core\Processing\Benchmarks\ProcessorPoolingBenchmark.cs
############################################################
    1: using System;
    2: using System.Diagnostics;
    3: using WildsEngine.Core.Abstractions;
    4: using WildsEngine.Core.Pooling;
    5: using WildsEngine.Core.Processing.Processor;
    6: 
    7: namespace WildsEngine.Benchmarks
    8: {
    9:     /// <summary>
   10:     /// Compares direct TaskProcessor allocation against
   11:     /// pooled TaskProcessor leasing.
   12:     /// </summary>
   13:     public sealed class ProcessorPoolingBenchmark
   14:     {
   15:         private readonly IComponent _component;
   16:         private readonly ITaskRegistry _registry;
   17: 
   18:         public ProcessorPoolingBenchmark(
   19:             IComponent component,
   20:             ITaskRegistry registry)
   21:         {
   22:             _component = component ??
   23:                 throw new ArgumentNullException(
   24:                     nameof(component));
   25: 
   26:             _registry = registry ??
   27:                 throw new ArgumentNullException(
   28:                     nameof(registry));
   29:         }
   30: 
   31:         public ProcessorPoolingBenchmarkResult Run(
   32:             int iterations,
   33:             int maximumRetained = 64,
   34:             int maximumConcurrent = 64)
   35:         {
   36:             if (iterations <= 0)
   37:             {
   38:                 throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(
   39:                     nameof(iterations));
   40:             }
   41: 
   42:             if (maximumRetained < 0)
   43:             {
   44:                 throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(
   45:                     nameof(maximumRetained));
   46:             }
   47: 
   48:             if (maximumConcurrent <= 0)
   49:             {
   50:                 throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(
   51:                     nameof(maximumConcurrent));
   52:             }
   53: 
   54:             WarmUp();
   55: 
   56:             var allocationMeasurementAvailable =
   57:                 IsAllocationMeasurementAvailable();
   58: 
   59:             var directAllocatedBytesBefore =
   60:                 GetAllocatedBytes();
   61: 
   62:             var directWatch =
   63:                 Stopwatch.StartNew();
   64: 
   65:             for (var i = 0; i < iterations; i++)
   66:             {
   67:                 var processor =
   68:                     new TaskProcessor(
   69:                         _component,
   70:                         "benchmark.direct",
   71:                         _registry);
   72: 
   73:                 Consume(
   74:                     processor);
   75:             }
   76: 
   77:             directWatch.Stop();
   78: 
   79:             var directAllocatedBytes =
   80:                 allocationMeasurementAvailable
   81:                     ? GetAllocatedBytes() -
   82:                       directAllocatedBytesBefore
   83:                     : 0;
   84: 
   85:             using (var pool =
   86:                 new ObjectPool<ITaskProcessor>(
   87:                     factory: () =>
   88:                         new TaskProcessor(
   89:                             _component,
   90:                             "benchmark.pooled",
   91:                             _registry),
   92:                     maximumRetained:
   93:                         maximumRetained,
   94:                     maximumConcurrent:
   95:                         maximumConcurrent))
   96:             {
   97:                 var pooledAllocatedBytesBefore =
   98:                     GetAllocatedBytes();
   99: 
  100:                 var pooledWatch =
  101:                     Stopwatch.StartNew();
  102: 
  103:                 for (var i = 0; i < iterations; i++)
  104:                 {
  105:                     using (var lease = pool.Rent())
  106:                     {
  107:                         Consume(
  108:                             lease.Instance);
  109:                     }
  110:                 }
  111: 
  112:                 pooledWatch.Stop();
  113: 
  114:                 var pooledAllocatedBytes =
  115:                     allocationMeasurementAvailable
  116:                         ? GetAllocatedBytes() -
  117:                           pooledAllocatedBytesBefore
  118:                         : 0;
  119: 
  120:                 return new ProcessorPoolingBenchmarkResult(
  121:                     iterations,
  122:                     directWatch.Elapsed,
  123:                     pooledWatch.Elapsed,
  124:                     directAllocatedBytes,
  125:                     pooledAllocatedBytes,
  126:                     pool.CreatedCount,
  127:                     allocationMeasurementAvailable);
  128:             }
  129:         }
  130: 
  131:         private void WarmUp()
  132:         {
  133:             for (var i = 0; i < 128; i++)
  134:             {
  135:                 var processor =
  136:                     new TaskProcessor(
  137:                         _component,
  138:                         "benchmark.warmup",
  139:                         _registry);
  140: 
  141:                 Consume(
  142:                     processor);
  143:             }
  144:         }
  145: 
  146:         private static bool IsAllocationMeasurementAvailable()
  147:         {
  148: #if NETSTANDARD2_1
  149:             return true;
  150: #else
  151:             return false;
  152: #endif
  153:         }
  154: 
  155:         private static long GetAllocatedBytes()
  156:         {
  157: #if NETSTANDARD2_1
  158:             return GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread();
  159: #else
  160:             return 0;
  161: #endif
  162:         }
  163: 
  164:         private static void Consume(
  165:             ITaskProcessor processor)
  166:         {
  167:             if (processor == null)
  168:             {
  169:                 throw new InvalidOperationException();
  170:             }
  171:         }
  172:     }
  173: }

    1: using System;
    2: 
    3: namespace WildsEngine.Benchmarks
    4: {
    5:     /// <summary>
    6:     /// Contains the results of a processor pooling benchmark.

    8:     public sealed class ProcessorPoolingBenchmarkResult

   10:         public ProcessorPoolingBenchmarkResult(
   11:             int iterations,

   56:                 $"Direct duration: {DirectDuration.TotalMilliseconds:F3} ms{Environment.NewLine}" +
   57:                 $"Pooled duration: {PooledDuration.TotalMilliseconds:F3} ms{Environment.NewLine}" +

FILE: WildsEngine.Core\Processing\Coordinator\PulseCoordinator.cs
############################################################
    1: using System;
    2: using System.Collections.Generic;
    3: using System.Linq;
    4: using WildsEngine.Core.Abstractions;
    5: using WildsEngine.Core.Units;
    6: 
    7: namespace WildsEngine.Core.Processing.Coordinator
    8: {
    9:     /// <summary>
   10:     /// Coordinates all required WorkUnits for one Pulse.
   11:     ///
   12:     /// The coordinator prevents early completion and records
   13:     /// successful, failed, and cancelled Pulse outcomes.
   14:     /// </summary>
   15:     public sealed class PulseCoordinator :
   16:         IPulseCoordinator
   17:     {
   18:         private readonly object _sync =
   19:             new object();
   20: 
   21:         private readonly List<IWorkUnit> _workUnits =
   22:             new List<IWorkUnit>();
   23: 
   24:         private readonly HashSet<Guid> _workUnitIds =
   25:             new HashSet<Guid>();
   26: 
   27:         public PulseCoordinator(
   28:             IPulse pulse)
   29:         {
   30:             Pulse = pulse ??
   31:                 throw new ArgumentNullException(
   32:                     nameof(pulse));
   33:         }
   34: 
   35:         public IPulse Pulse { get; }
   36: 
   37:         public int WorkUnitCount
   38:         {
   39:             get
   40:             {
   41:                 lock (_sync)
   42:                 {
   43:                     return _workUnits.Count;
   44:                 }
   45:             }
   46:         }
   47: 
   48:         public IReadOnlyList<IWorkUnit> WorkUnits
   49:         {
   50:             get
   51:             {
   52:                 lock (_sync)
   53:                 {
   54:                     return _workUnits.ToArray();
   55:                 }
   56:             }
   57:         }
   58: 
   59:         public bool CanResolve
   60:         {
   61:             get
   62:             {
   63:                 lock (_sync)
   64:                 {
   65:                     return CanResolveCore();
   66:                 }
   67:             }
   68:         }
   69: 
   70:         public bool CanFinalize
   71:         {
   72:             get
   73:             {
   74:                 lock (_sync)
   75:                 {
   76:                     return CanFinalizeCore();
   77:                 }
   78:             }
   79:         }
   80: 
   81:         public bool AddWorkUnit(
   82:             IWorkUnit workUnit)
   83:         {
   84:             if (workUnit == null)
   85:             {
   86:                 throw new ArgumentNullException(
   87:                     nameof(workUnit));
   88:             }
   89: 
   90:             if (workUnit.PulseId != Pulse.Id)
   91:             {
   92:                 return false;
   93:             }
   94: 
   95:             lock (_sync)
   96:             {
   97:                 if (Pulse.IsTerminal)
   98:                 {
   99:                     return false;
  100:                 }
  101: 
  102:                 if (!_workUnitIds.Add(
  103:                         workUnit.Id))
  104:                 {
  105:                     return false;
  106:                 }
  107: 
  108:                 _workUnits.Add(
  109:                     workUnit);
  110: 
  111:                 return true;
  112:             }
  113:         }
  114: 
  115:         public bool TryResolve(
  116:             object? result,
  117:             out IMoment? moment)
  118:         {
  119:             lock (_sync)
  120:             {
  121:                 moment = null;
  122: 
  123:                 if (!CanResolveCore())
  124:                 {
  125:                     return false;
  126:                 }
  127: 
  128:                 return TryCreateCompletedMoment(
  129:                     result,
  130:                     out moment);
  131:             }
  132:         }
  133: 
  134:         public bool TryFinalize(
  135:             object? result,
  136:             out IMoment? moment)
  137:         {
  138:             lock (_sync)
  139:             {
  140:                 moment = null;
  141: 
  142:                 if (!CanFinalizeCore())
  143:                 {
  144:                     return false;
  145:                 }
  146: 
  147:                 var failedWork =
  148:                     GetFirstFailedWorkUnit();
  149: 
  150:                 if (failedWork != null)
  151:                 {
  152:                     return TryCreateFailedMoment(
  153:                         failedWork,
  154:                         out moment);
  155:                 }
  156: 
  157:                 if (ContainsCancelledWorkUnit())
  158:                 {
  159:                     return TryCreateCancelledMoment(
  160:                         out moment);
  161:                 }
  162: 
  163:                 return TryCreateCompletedMoment(
  164:                     result,
  165:                     out moment);
  166:             }
  167:         }
  168: 
  169:         private bool TryCreateCompletedMoment(
  170:             object? result,
  171:             out IMoment? moment)
  172:         {
  173:             moment = null;
  174: 
  175:             if (!CanResolveCore())
  176:             {
  177:                 return false;
  178:             }
  179: 
  180:             if (!Pulse.TryComplete())
  181:             {
  182:                 return false;
  183:             }
  184: 
  185:             moment =
  186:                 new Moment(
  187:                     Pulse.Id,
  188:                     MomentOutcome.Completed,
  189:                     result,
  190:                     null,
  191:                     GetWorkUnitIds());
  192: 
  193:             return true;
  194:         }
  195: 
  196:         private bool TryCreateFailedMoment(
  197:             IWorkUnit failedWork,
  198:             out IMoment? moment)
  199:         {
  200:             moment = null;
  201: 
  202:             var exception =
  203:                 failedWork.Exception;
  204: 
  205:             if (exception == null)
  206:             {
  207:                 return false;
  208:             }
  209: 
  210:             if (!Pulse.TryFail())
  211:             {
  212:                 return false;
  213:             }
  214: 
  215:             moment =
  216:                 new Moment(
  217:                     Pulse.Id,
  218:                     MomentOutcome.Failed,
  219:                     null,
  220:                     exception,
  221:                     GetWorkUnitIds());
  222: 
  223:             return true;
  224:         }
  225: 
  226:         private bool TryCreateCancelledMoment(
  227:             out IMoment? moment)
  228:         {
  229:             moment = null;
  230: 
  231:             if (!Pulse.TryCancel())
  232:             {
  233:                 return false;
  234:             }
  235: 
  236:             moment =
  237:                 new Moment(
  238:                     Pulse.Id,
  239:                     MomentOutcome.Cancelled,
  240:                     null,
  241:                     null,
  242:                     GetWorkUnitIds());
  243: 
  244:             return true;
  245:         }
  246: 
  247:         private bool CanResolveCore()
  248:         {
  249:             if (Pulse.Status !=
  250:                 PulseStatus.Processing)
  251:             {
  252:                 return false;
  253:             }
  254: 
  255:             if (_workUnits.Count == 0)
  256:             {
  257:                 return false;
  258:             }
  259: 
  260:             for (
  261:                 var index = 0;
  262:                 index < _workUnits.Count;
  263:                 index++)
  264:             {
  265:                 if (_workUnits[index].Status !=
  266:                     WorkUnitStatus.Completed)
  267:                 {
  268:                     return false;
  269:                 }
  270:             }
  271: 
  272:             return true;
  273:         }
  274: 
  275:         private bool CanFinalizeCore()
  276:         {
  277:             if (Pulse.Status !=
  278:                 PulseStatus.Processing)
  279:             {
  280:                 return false;
  281:             }
  282: 
  283:             if (_workUnits.Count == 0)
  284:             {
  285:                 return false;
  286:             }
  287: 
  288:             for (
  289:                 var index = 0;
  290:                 index < _workUnits.Count;
  291:                 index++)
  292:             {
  293:                 if (!_workUnits[index].IsTerminal)
  294:                 {
  295:                     return false;
  296:                 }
  297:             }
  298: 
  299:             return true;
  300:         }
  301: 
  302:         private IWorkUnit? GetFirstFailedWorkUnit()
  303:         {
  304:             for (
  305:                 var index = 0;
  306:                 index < _workUnits.Count;
  307:                 index++)
  308:             {
  309:                 var workUnit =
  310:                     _workUnits[index];
  311: 
  312:                 if (workUnit.Status ==
  313:                     WorkUnitStatus.Failed)
  314:                 {
  315:                     return workUnit;
  316:                 }
  317:             }
  318: 
  319:             return null;
  320:         }
  321: 
  322:         private bool ContainsCancelledWorkUnit()
  323:         {
  324:             for (
  325:                 var index = 0;
  326:                 index < _workUnits.Count;
  327:                 index++)
  328:             {
  329:                 if (_workUnits[index].Status ==
  330:                     WorkUnitStatus.Cancelled)
  331:                 {
  332:                     return true;
  333:                 }
  334:             }
  335: 
  336:             return false;
  337:         }
  338: 
  339:         private Guid[] GetWorkUnitIds()
  340:         {
  341:             return _workUnits
  342:                 .Select(
  343:                     workUnit =>
  344:                         workUnit.Id)
  345:                 .ToArray();
  346:         }
  347:     }
  348: }

FILE: WildsEngine.Core\Processing\Processor\TaskProcessor.cs
############################################################
    1: using System;
    2: using WildsEngine.Core.Abstractions;
    3: 
    4: namespace WildsEngine.Core.Processing.Processor
    5: {
    6:     /// <summary>
    7:     /// Processes task work using a task registry.
    8:     /// Provides the task lifecycle boundary used by
    9:     /// pooled task processors.
   10:     /// </summary>
   11:     public class TaskProcessor :
   12:         ProcessorBase,
   13:         ITaskProcessor
   14:     {
   15:         public TaskProcessor(
   16:             IComponent component,
   17:             string layer,
   18:             ITaskRegistry registry)
   19:             : base(
   20:                 component,
   21:                 layer)
   22:         {
   23:             Registry = registry ??
   24:                 throw new ArgumentNullException(
   25:                     nameof(registry));
   26:         }
   27: 
   28:         public ITaskRegistry Registry { get; }
   29: 
   30:         /// <summary>
   31:         /// Parks a task for processing.
   32:         /// </summary>
   33:         public bool RegisterTask(
   34:             ITask task)
   35:         {
   36:             if (task == null)
   37:             {
   38:                 throw new ArgumentNullException(
   39:                     nameof(task));
   40:             }
   41: 
   42:             return Registry.Register(
   43:                 task);
   44:         }
   45: 
   46:         /// <summary>
   47:         /// Determines whether a task is currently parked.
   48:         /// </summary>
   49:         public bool ContainsTask(
   50:             Guid id)
   51:         {
   52:             return Registry.Contains(
   53:                 id);
   54:         }
   55: 
   56:         /// <summary>
   57:         /// Retrieves a parked task by identity.
   58:         /// </summary>
   59:         public ITask? GetTask(
   60:             Guid id)
   61:         {
   62:             return Registry.Get(
   63:                 id);
   64:         }
   65: 
   66:         /// <summary>
   67:         /// Attempts to retrieve a parked task by identity.
   68:         /// </summary>
   69:         public bool TryGetTask(
   70:             Guid id,
   71:             out ITask? task)
   72:         {
   73:             return Registry.TryGet(
   74:                 id,
   75:                 out task);
   76:         }
   77: 
   78:         /// <summary>
   79:         /// Removes a parked task after processing completes.
   80:         /// </summary>
   81:         public bool RemoveTask(
   82:             Guid id)
   83:         {
   84:             return Registry.Remove(
   85:                 id);
   86:         }
   87: 
   88:         /// <summary>
   89:         /// Clears transient processor state before this
   90:         /// processor is returned to its pool.
   91:         ///
   92:         /// Registry contents intentionally survive processor
   93:         /// reuse because task lifetime is independent from
   94:         /// processor lifetime.
   95:         /// </summary>
   96:         protected override bool OnReset()
   97:         {
   98:             return true;
   99:         }
  100:     }
  101: }

   55: 
   56:         public abstract bool Process(
   57:             IStateInstruction instruction);
   58: 
   59:         /// <summary>
   60:         /// Processes Neighbor-topology instructions that are
   61:         /// common to all Wilds states.
   62:         ///
   63:         /// Concrete states should invoke this before handling
   64:         /// state-specific instruction types.
   65:         /// </summary>
   66:         protected bool TryProcessNeighborInstruction(
   67:             IStateInstruction instruction)
   68:         {
   69:             if (instruction == null)
   70:             {
   71:                 throw new ArgumentNullException(
   72:                     nameof(instruction));
   73:             }
   74: 
   75:             if (instruction is
   76:                 AddNeighborInstruction addNeighbor)
   77:             {
   78:                 return Component.Neighbors.Add(
   79:                     addNeighbor.Neighbor,
   80:                     addNeighbor.Membership,
   81:                     addNeighbor.Distance);
   82:             }
   83: 
   84:             if (instruction is
   85:                 RemoveNeighborInstruction removeNeighbor)
   86:             {
   87:                 return Component.Neighbors.Remove(
   88:                     removeNeighbor.NeighborId,
   89:                     removeNeighbor.Membership);
   90:             }
   91: 
   92:             if (instruction is
   93:                 SetNeighborDistanceInstruction setDistance)
   94:             {
   95:                 return Component.Neighbors.SetDistance(
   96:                     setDistance.NeighborId,
   97:                     setDistance.Membership,
   98:                     setDistance.Distance);
   99:             }
  100: 
  101:             return false;
  102:         }
  103:     }
  104: }

  107:             if (pulseId == Guid.Empty)
  108:             {
  109:                 throw new ArgumentException(
  110:                     "Moments require a non-empty Pulse ID.",
  111:                     nameof(pulseId));
  112:             }
  113: 
  114:             return pulseId;
  115:         }
  116: 
  117:         private static void ValidateOutcome(
  118:             MomentOutcome outcome,
  119:             Exception? exception)
  120:         {
  121:             if (outcome ==
  122:                 MomentOutcome.Failed &&
  123:                 exception == null)
  124:             {
  125:                 throw new ArgumentException(
  126:                     "Failed Moments require an exception.",
  127:                     nameof(exception));
  128:             }
  129: 
  130:             if (outcome !=
  131:                 MomentOutcome.Failed &&
  132:                 exception != null)
  133:             {
  134:                 throw new ArgumentException(
  135:                     "Only failed Moments may carry an exception.",
  136:                     nameof(exception));
  137:             }
  138:         }
  139: 
  140:         private static IReadOnlyList<Guid>
  141:             CopyWorkUnitIds(
  142:                 IEnumerable<Guid>? workUnitIds)
  143:         {
  144:             if (workUnitIds == null)
  145:             {
  146:                 return Array.Empty<Guid>();
  147:             }
  148: 
  149:             var copy =
  150:                 workUnitIds
  151:                     .Where(
  152:                         id => id != Guid.Empty)
  153:                     .Distinct()
  154:                     .ToArray();
  155: 
  156:             return copy.Length == 0
  157:                 ? Array.Empty<Guid>()
  158:                 : copy;
  159:         }
  160:     }

    1: using System;
    2: using WildsEngine.Core.Abstractions;
    3: 
    4: namespace WildsEngine.Core.Units
    5: {
    6:     /// <summary>
    7:     /// Represents one complete consumer request.
    8:     ///
    9:     /// The pulse identity is the canonical correlation

   28: 
   29:             _status =

   31:         }

   53:                     return _status;
   54:                 }
   55:             }
   56:         }

   58:         public bool IsTerminal

   66:                 }

   72:             return TryTransition(
   73:                 PulseStatus.Created,
   74:                 PulseStatus.Decomposing);
   75:         }

   78:         {
   79:             return TryTransition(
   80:                 PulseStatus.Decomposing,
   81:                 PulseStatus.Pending);

   89:         }

   92:         {
   93:             return TryTransition(
   94:                 PulseStatus.Ready,
   95:                 PulseStatus.Processing);
   96:         }
   97: 
   98:         public bool TryComplete()

  102:                 PulseStatus.Completed);

  115:         }

  118:             PulseStatus expected,
  119:             PulseStatus next)

  121:             lock (_sync)

  128:                 _status = next;
  129: 
  130:                 return true;

FILE: WildsEngine.Qsl\WildsQslExecutionException.cs
############################################################
    1: using System;
    2: using QSL.Core;
    3: 
    4: namespace WildsEngine.Qsl
    5: {
    6:     /// <summary>
    7:     /// Represents an unsuccessful QSL processing result
    8:     /// encountered while resolving a Wilds WorkUnit.
    9:     ///
   10:     /// Throwing this exception allows WildsEngine to record
   11:     /// the QSL failure as a failed WorkUnit, failed Pulse,
   12:     /// and failed Moment.
   13:     /// </summary>
   14:     public sealed class WildsQslExecutionException :
   15:         Exception
   16:     {
   17:         public WildsQslExecutionException(
   18:             QslProcessingResult result)
   19:             : base(
   20:                 CreateMessage(
   21:                     result),
   22:                 result != null
   23:                     ? result.Exception
   24:                     : null)
   25:         {
   26:             Result = result ??
   27:                 throw new ArgumentNullException(
   28:                     nameof(result));
   29:         }
   30: 
   31:         public QslProcessingResult Result { get; }
   32: 
   33:         private static string CreateMessage(
   34:             QslProcessingResult result)
   35:         {
   36:             if (result == null)
   37:             {
   38:                 return "QSL processing failed without a result.";
   39:             }
   40: 
   41:             if (result.HasException &&
   42:                 result.Exception != null)
   43:             {
   44:                 return
   45:                     "QSL processing raised an exception: " +
   46:                     result.Exception.Message;
   47:             }
   48: 
   49:             if (result.ParseFailed)
   50:             {
   51:                 return
   52:                     "QSL parsing failed with " +
   53:                     result.ParserDiagnostics.Count +
   54:                     " diagnostic(s).";
   55:             }
   56: 
   57:             if (result.EvaluationFailed)
   58:             {
   59:                 return
   60:                     "QSL evaluation failed with " +
   61:                     result.RuntimeDiagnostics.Count +
   62:                     " runtime diagnostic(s).";
   63:             }
   64: 
   65:             return "QSL processing did not succeed.";
   66:         }
   67:     }
   68: }

FILE: WildsEngine.Qsl\WildsQslExecutor.cs
############################################################
    1: using System;
    2: using System.Threading;
    3: using System.Threading.Tasks;
    4: using QSL.Core;
    5: using WildsEngine.Core.Abstractions;
    6: 
    7: namespace WildsEngine.Qsl
    8: {
    9:     /// <summary>
   10:     /// Executes QSL requests through the complete
   11:     /// WildsEngine request lifecycle.
   12:     ///
   13:     /// request
   14:     ///     -> Pulse
   15:     ///     -> WorkUnit
   16:     ///     -> QSL preparation
   17:     ///     -> QSL evaluation
   18:     ///     -> Moment
   19:     ///     -> Timeline
   20:     ///     -> Epoch
   21:     ///
   22:     /// Wilds owns the processing and temporal lifecycle.
   23:     /// QSL owns consumer binding, attached state,
   24:     /// language evaluation, diagnostics, and provenance.
   25:     /// </summary>
   26:     public sealed class WildsQslExecutor
   27:     {
   28:         private readonly QslEngine _qsl;
   29: 
   30:         private readonly Core.WildsEngine _wilds;
   31: 
   32:         public WildsQslExecutor(
   33:             QslEngine qsl,
   34:             Core.WildsEngine wilds)
   35:         {
   36:             _qsl =
   37:                 qsl
   38:                 ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(
   39:                     nameof(qsl));
   40: 
   41:             _wilds =
   42:                 wilds
   43:                 ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(
   44:                     nameof(wilds));
   45:         }
   46: 
   47:         /// <summary>
   48:         /// Executes ordinary QSL source through Wilds.
   49:         ///
   50:         /// This overload preserves the existing
   51:         /// source-only integration path.
   52:         /// </summary>
   53:         public ValueTask<IMoment> ExecuteAsync(
   54:             string source,
   55:             CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
   56:         {
   57:             if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(
   58:                     source))
   59:             {
   60:                 throw new ArgumentException(
   61:                     "QSL source cannot be empty.",
   62:                     nameof(source));
   63:             }
   64: 
   65:             return _wilds.ExecuteAsync(
   66:                 source,
   67:                 ExecuteSourceAsync,
   68:                 cancellationToken);
   69:         }
   70: 
   71:         /// <summary>
   72:         /// Executes a complete QSL request containing
   73:         /// source, consumer bindings, and state packages
   74:         /// through Wilds.
   75:         /// </summary>
   76:         public ValueTask<IMoment> ExecuteAsync(
   77:             WildsQslRequest request,
   78:             CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
   79:         {
   80:             if (request == null)
   81:             {
   82:                 throw new ArgumentNullException(
   83:                     nameof(request));
   84:             }
   85: 
   86:             return _wilds.ExecuteAsync(
   87:                 request,
   88:                 ExecuteRequestAsync,
   89:                 cancellationToken);
   90:         }
   91: 
   92:         private ValueTask<object?> ExecuteSourceAsync(
   93:             object? request,
   94:             CancellationToken cancellationToken)
   95:         {
   96:             cancellationToken
   97:                 .ThrowIfCancellationRequested();
   98: 
   99:             var source =
  100:                 request as string;
  101: 
  102:             if (source == null)
  103:             {
  104:                 throw new InvalidOperationException(
  105:                     "WildsQslExecutor expected QSL source.");
  106:             }
  107: 
  108:             return EvaluateAsync(
  109:                 source);
  110:         }
  111: 
  112:         private ValueTask<object?> ExecuteRequestAsync(
  113:             object? request,
  114:             CancellationToken cancellationToken)
  115:         {
  116:             cancellationToken
  117:                 .ThrowIfCancellationRequested();
  118: 
  119:             var qslRequest =
  120:                 request as WildsQslRequest;
  121: 
  122:             if (qslRequest == null)
  123:             {
  124:                 throw new InvalidOperationException(
  125:                     "WildsQslExecutor expected a " +
  126:                     "WildsQslRequest.");
  127:             }
  128: 
  129:             for (
  130:                 var index = 0;
  131:                 index < qslRequest.Consumers.Count;
  132:                 index++)
  133:             {
  134:                 _qsl.BindConsumer(
  135:                     qslRequest.Consumers[index]);
  136:             }
  137: 
  138:             for (
  139:                 var index = 0;
  140:                 index < qslRequest.StatePackages.Count;
  141:                 index++)
  142:             {
  143:                 _qsl.ReceiveState(
  144:                     qslRequest.StatePackages[index]);
  145:             }
  146: 
  147:             cancellationToken
  148:                 .ThrowIfCancellationRequested();
  149: 
  150:             return EvaluateAsync(
  151:                 qslRequest.Source);
  152:         }
  153: 
  154:         private ValueTask<object?> EvaluateAsync(
  155:             string source)
  156:         {
  157:             var result =
  158:                 _qsl.Evaluate(
  159:                     source);
  160: 
  161:             if (!result.Succeeded)
  162:             {
  163:                 throw new WildsQslExecutionException(
  164:                     result);
  165:             }
  166: 
  167:             return new ValueTask<object?>(
  168:                 result.Value);
  169:         }
  170:     }
  171: }

############################################################
FILE: WildsEngine.Qsl\WildsQslRequest.cs
############################################################
    1: using System;
    2: using System.Collections.Generic;
    3: using QSL.Core.Runtime.Context;
    4: using QSL.Core.Runtime.Packages;
    5: 
    6: namespace WildsEngine.Qsl
    7: {
    8:     /// <summary>
    9:     /// Represents one complete QSL request submitted
   10:     /// through the Wilds processing lifecycle.
   11:     ///
   12:     /// Wilds treats this request as opaque runtime data.
   13:     /// The Wilds/QSL integration layer prepares QSL from
   14:     /// the supplied consumer bindings, state packages,
   15:     /// and source.
   16:     /// </summary>
   17:     public sealed class WildsQslRequest
   18:     {
   19:         private readonly QslConsumerBinding[] _consumers;
   20: 
   21:         private readonly QslStatePackage[] _statePackages;
   22: 
   23:         public WildsQslRequest(
   24:             string source,
   25:             IEnumerable<QslConsumerBinding>? consumers = null,
   26:             IEnumerable<QslStatePackage>? statePackages = null)
   27:         {
   28:             if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(
   29:                     source))
   30:             {
   31:                 throw new ArgumentException(
   32:                     "QSL source cannot be empty.",
   33:                     nameof(source));
   34:             }
   35: 
   36:             Source =
   37:                 source;
   38: 
   39:             _consumers =
   40:                 Copy(
   41:                     consumers,
   42:                     nameof(consumers));
   43: 
   44:             _statePackages =
   45:                 Copy(
   46:                     statePackages,
   47:                     nameof(statePackages));
   48:         }
   49: 
   50:         public string Source { get; }
   51: 
   52:         public IReadOnlyList<QslConsumerBinding> Consumers =>
   53:             _consumers;
   54: 
   55:         public IReadOnlyList<QslStatePackage> StatePackages =>
   56:             _statePackages;
   57: 
   58:         private static T[] Copy<T>(
   59:             IEnumerable<T>? values,
   60:             string parameterName)
   61:             where T : class
   62:         {
   63:             if (values == null)
   64:             {
   65:                 return Array.Empty<T>();
   66:             }
   67: 
   68:             var items =
   69:                 new List<T>();
   70: 
   71:             foreach (var value in values)
   72:             {
   73:                 if (value == null)
   74:                 {
   75:                     throw new ArgumentException(
   76:                         "Request collections cannot contain null.",
   77:                         parameterName);
   78:                 }
   79: 
   80:                 items.Add(
   81:                     value);
   82:             }
   83: 
   84:             return items.ToArray();
   85:         }
   86:     }
   87: }

   63: 
   64: Consumer terminology
   65: 
   66: A consumer-owned object is a participant in Wilds. It is not permanently classified as an emission source or receiver.
   67: 
   68: Source and receiving roles describe a consumer-owned object's position in a particular emission interaction. They do not define separate Wilds Core entity types.
   69: 
   70: A participating consumer-owned object may:
   71: 
   72: expose state that contributes to emission resolution;
   73: participate in Neighbor topology;
   74: expose emitter behavior and emission rules;
   75: receive propagated facts through its relationships;
   76: participate in eligibility evaluation;
   77: have ordinary Wilds instructions resolved from eligible facts;
   78: participate in Wilds processing;
   79: later serve as the source participant in another emission interaction.
   80: 
   81: The same consumer-owned object can therefore participate on either side of different interactions without changing its architectural identity.
   82: 
   83: Wilds owns the generic relationship, emission, instruction, processing, lifecycle, and history mechanics. The consumer retains ownership of domain objects, vocabulary, state, policies, and semantic meaning.

FILE: WildsEngine.Core\Docs\readme.updated.md
############################################################
    1: # Wilds Engine
    2: 
    3: Wilds is a reusable game-simulation and processing engine. It coordinates work, state, relationships, and history without knowing the game-specific meaning of the objects it processes.
    4: 
    5: Wilds Core stays independent of Unity, QSL, Cryo Nation, and consumer-specific entities or rules. Consumer-owned values can live in component metadata and processing context without becoming Wilds Core types.
    6: 
    7: ## Runtime model
    8: 
    9: Wilds uses a unified work and temporal model:
   10: 
   11: ```text
   12: BaseUnit
   13:   |- Pulse      coordinated request
   14:   |- WorkUnit   required work belonging to a Pulse
   15:   |- Moment     resolved Pulse outcome
   16:   |- Timeline   Moment history ordered by successful commit
   17:   `- Epoch      collection of Timelines
   18: ```
   19: 
   20: A Pulse owns its required WorkUnits and cannot resolve successfully until the required work resolves honestly. Failed or canceled work cannot silently become a successful Pulse.
   21: 
   22: ```text
   23: Consumer request
   24:       |
   25:       v
   26:     Pulse
   27:       |
   28:       +----> WorkUnit
   29:       +----> WorkUnit
   30:       `----> WorkUnit
   31:                |
   32:                v
   33:         Pulse resolution
   34:                |
   35:                v
   36:             Moment
   37:                |
   38:                v
   39:            Timeline
   40:                |
   41:                v
   42:              Epoch
   43: ```
   44: 
   45: The route can retain arbitrary consumer runtime-object references. Wilds coordinates the work and history; it does not need to understand the concrete game type carried by the result.
   46: 
   47: For concurrent executions, Timeline order is the serialized order in which terminal Moments are successfully committed. Wilds does not guarantee request-submission order, Pulse-creation order, operation-completion order, or pre-commit finalization order across concurrent requests.
   48: 
   49: ## Processing infrastructure
   50: 
   51: Wilds provides the lower-level machinery used by the execution route:
   52: 
   53: - components, state, context, signals, and metadata;
   54: - state instructions and tasks;
   55: - instruction and task registries;
   56: - component-bound processors;
   57: - bounded processor pools;
   58: - engine composition and lifecycle management.
   59: 
   60: Processor lifetime remains independent of registered work lifetime. Work can therefore survive the processor lease that happened to execute it.
   61: 
   62: ## QSL integration
   63: 
   64: Wilds is the exposed consumer surface. QSL integration lives in the companion WildsEngine.Qsl project rather than Wilds Core, and QSL performs delegated computation inside a Wilds-owned request lifecycle.
   65: 
   66: ```text
   67: Consumer
   68:    |
   69:    v
   70: Wilds
   71:    |
   72:    v
   73: Pulse
   74:    |
   75:    v
   76: WorkUnit
   77:    |
   78:    v
   79: Wilds/QSL integration
   80:    |
   81:    +--> consumer bindings
   82:    +--> attached state packages
   83:    `--> QSL source
   84:             |
   85:             v
   86:        QSL computation
   87:             |
   88:             v
   89:          result
   90:             |
   91:             v
   92:    WorkUnit completion
   93:             |
   94:             v
   95:          Moment
   96:             |
   97:             v
   98:         Timeline
   99:             |
  100:             v
  101:           Epoch
  102: ```
  103: 
  104: Wilds creates the Pulse and WorkUnit before QSL evaluates the request. QSL's result returns to Wilds, which completes the WorkUnit and resolves the Pulse into its terminal Moment.
  105: 
  106: WildsQslRequest is the certified request envelope for QSL-backed work. It carries QSL source, exact consumer bindings, and attached state packages through Wilds as opaque request data. WildsQslExecutor bridges the Wilds lifecycle to QslEngine; it is integration machinery, not the conceptual consumer front door.
  107: 
  108: QSL processes the valid source and runtime context it is given. Propagation is independent: a QSL-backed request may be processed locally without requiring its outcome to propagate.
  109: 
  110: The canonical integration proof is:
  111: 
  112: ```text
  113: player.Health = player.Health - (action.Amount * (action.SpaceDustAppetite / 100))
  114: ```
  115: 
  116: With `player.Health = 50`, native `action.Amount = 10`, and attached `action.SpaceDustAppetite = 87`, the certified route mutates the exact consumer-owned Player to `41.3`, then records the result through Wilds history.
  117: 
  118: ## Certification
  119: 
  120: The certification surfaces are complementary:
  121: 
  122: - **QSL core through Wilds:** 156/156 cases pass with zero failures and zero missing dependencies.
  123: - **Wilds/QSL request envelope:** passes envelope execution, exact consumer binding, attached-state composition, and the Space Dust 50 -> 41.3 mutation.
  124: - **Wilds/QSL end-to-end:** proves that Wilds establishes the request lifecycle, delegates QSL-backed work, receives the QSL result, then completes the WorkUnit and resolves the terminal Moment.
  125: - **Emission Gates 1-6:** focused emitter regression passes 67/67 before the final Gate 6 topology-snapshot additions; the final Gate 6 suite passes 13/13. Gates 4-6 certify immutable resolved carriers, arbitrary N-dimensional normalized propagation, received-value eligibility, complete provenance continuity, and historical stability after topology changes.
  126: - **Full Core regression:** 165/165 passes when run serialized. The Wilds/QSL end-to-end lifecycle also passes 20/20 in isolated repetition. One earlier parallel full-suite run produced a single intermittent Wilds/QSL end-to-end failure; this is tracked as test-suite parallel-isolation behavior rather than an emission semantic failure.
  127: 
  128: Expected-error QSL cases still produce failed Moments when failure is the correct runtime outcome. Certification success and runtime outcome remain intentionally separate concepts.
  129: 
  130: The older consumer-dependent corpus remains useful as conformance material, but it no longer defines the architectural requirement that QSL itself be the consumer-facing simulation surface. The certified request-envelope path demonstrates that consumer-owned objects and attached vocabulary can be processed through Wilds without moving consumer concepts into Wilds Core.
  131: 
  132: Known unrelated warnings remain separate from the emission gates: CS8604 in `NeighborTraversal.cs` and existing xUnit analyzer warnings for `ConfigureAwait(false)` in test methods.
  133: 
  134: ## Neighbor topology and membership model
  135: 
  136: Wilds objects can participate in directional Neighbor relationships.
  137: 
  138: A Neighbor is not limited to an immediately adjacent object. A Neighbor is another member of a shared relational collection or topology, with distance describing proximity inside that relationship.
  139: 
  140: **Membership establishes neighborhood. Distance establishes proximity. Adjacency is the special case where distance is 1.**
  141: 
  142: Relationship identity is defined by:
  143: 
  144: ```text
  145: Neighbor.Id + Membership
  146: ```
  147: 
  148: Distance is relationship state rather than relationship identity and may change without replacing the relationship.
  149: 
  150: Neighbor relationships are directional:
  151: 
  152: ```text
  153: A -> B
  154: ```
  155: 
  156: does not imply:
  157: 
  158: ```text
  159: B -> A
  160: ```
  161: 
  162: If both relationships exist, they remain independently mutable.
  163: 
  164: The same Neighbor may also participate through multiple memberships:
  165: 
  166: ```text
  167: A
  168: |
  169: +-- B : local
  170: |
  171: `-- B : remote
  172: ```
  173: 
  174: Those relationships remain independent even though they reference the same Neighbor object.
  175: 
  176: Wilds provides reusable topology operations over relationship snapshots, including filtering, ordering, grouping, sampling, and scalar computations. Topology operators observe or transform snapshots without owning or mutating the source Neighbor collection.
  177: 
  178: Distance is intentionally abstract. Depending on the consumer and topology, it may represent hops, cells, traversal depth, semantic separation, or another consumer-defined metric.
  179: 
  180: Wilds owns the relationship mechanics. The consumer owns the meaning of the relationship and its distance metric.
  181: 
  182: ## Neighbor propagation and eligibility
  183: 
  184: Wilds can interpret Neighbor distance through a propagation policy without assigning consumer-specific meaning to the propagated value.
  185: 
  186: The current exponential distance-propagation model is:
  187: 
  188: ```text
  189: Iout = Iin * exp(-k * d)
  190: ```
  191: 
  192: where:
  193: 
  194: - `Iin` is source intensity;
  195: - `d` is Neighbor relationship distance;
  196: - `k` is configured decay;
  197: - `Iout` is resulting propagated intensity.
  198: 
  199: Propagation remains separate from topology. Neighbor topology owns relationship distance; propagation policy determines how that distance affects an intensity.
  200: 
  201: Direct scalar propagation preserves the authoritative resolved magnitude and does not claim normalization. Vector propagation first groups an ordered set of same-source resolved emissions into an immutable `IResolvedEmissionVector`, normalizes that set into an immutable `INormalizedEmissionVector`, and then produces an immutable `IPropagatedEmissionVector`.
  202: 
  203: ```text
  204: resolved emissions
  205:         |
  206:         v
  207: IResolvedEmissionVector
  208:         |
  209:         v
  210: normalization policy
  211:         |
  212:         v
  213: INormalizedEmissionVector
  214:         |
  215:         v
  216: Neighbor propagation
  217:         |
  218:         v
  219: IPropagatedEmissionVector
  220: ```
  221: 
  222: The vector route supports arbitrary dimension `N`. It preserves exact emitter identity, component identity and ordering, consumer-owned channel names, resolved magnitudes, normalized magnitudes, received magnitudes, exact relationship identity, and the propagation distance used during evaluation. Duplicate channel names and mixed-source vectors are rejected. Caller-owned collections are snapshotted and exposed through read-only wrappers.
  223: 
  224: Eligibility is evaluated separately from attenuation. Gate 6 evaluates the received propagated `Value`, never the stronger resolved magnitude or the pre-attenuation normalized magnitude. The minimum-intensity boundary remains inclusive:
  225: 
  226: ```text
  227: received value < threshold    -> not eligible
  228: received value = threshold    -> eligible
  229: received value > threshold    -> eligible
  230: ```
  231: 
  232: Scalar eligibility produces an immutable decision over one exact propagated emission. Vector eligibility evaluates every received component independently and preserves both eligible and ineligible channels. `EligibleCount`, `AnyEligible`, and `AllEligible` are descriptive summaries, not execution policy.
  233: 
  234: ```text
  235: IPropagatedEmissionVector
  236:         |
  237:         v
  238: eligibility policy
  239:         |
  240:         v
  241: IEmissionEligibilityVector
  242:         |
  243:         +-- eligible component decisions
  244:         `-- ineligible component decisions retained
  245: ```
  246: 
  247: Eligibility results remain historical facts. If live topology changes after propagation and eligibility, the exact propagated source, evaluated value, decision, original relationship reference, and frozen propagation distance remain unchanged. Eligibility does not mean that a receiver accepted the value, that state changed, or that an effect must occur.
  248: 
  249: The meaning of every channel and value remains consumer-owned. Wilds provides the mechanics for resolution, grouping, normalization, propagation, and qualification without interpreting consumer vocabulary.
  250: 
  251: ## Emission resolution
  252: 
  253: Wilds has a certified emitter model for deriving abstract magnitudes from consumer-owned data and the emitter's current relational context. Emission processing now has six certified gates:
  254: 
  255: ```text
  256: consumer-owned value
  257:         |
  258:         v
  259: base emission scalar
  260:         |
  261:         +---- current Neighbor topology
  262:         |              |
  263:         |              v
  264:         |       topology operators
  265:         |              |
  266:         |              v
  267:         |       topology scalar
  268:         |              |
  269:         +--------------+
  270:         |
  271:         v
  272: composition policy
  273:         |
  274:         v
  275: resolved emission
  276:         |
  277:         v
  278: immutable carrier / vector
  279:         |
  280:         v
  281: normalization when vectorized
  282:         |
  283:         v
  284: relationship propagation
  285:         |
  286:         v
  287: received propagated fact
  288:         |
  289:         v
  290: eligibility decision
  291: ```
  292: 
  293: The **base emission scalar** comes from consumer-owned data. The **topology scalar** comes from current Wilds relational context through the existing Neighbor operator system. The **composition policy** determines how those independent scalar inputs are combined. The **resolved emission scalar** is the authoritative output of emission resolution.
  294: 
  295: The current additive certification fixture proves:
  296: 
  297: ```text
  298: base emission scalar = 1.6
  299: topology scalar      = 2
  300: composition          = additive
  301: resolved emission    = 3.6
  302: ```
  303: 
  304: The value `2` is not itself the emission. It describes topology-derived context. Changing the selected topology can therefore change the resolved emission without changing the consumer-owned base value.
  305: 
  306: The certified route reuses the existing Neighbor abstractions rather than introducing an emitter-specific topology system. `NeighborPipeline` can compose topology-selection stages before scalar reduction, while `IEmissionComposition` keeps composition mathematics consumer-supplied.
  307: 
  308: ### Certified emission gates
  309: 
  310: - **Gate 1 - Emitter primitive:** consumer properties and named groups resolve into finite base emission scalars while the emitter remains an ordinary Wilds object with normal Neighbor topology.
  311: - **Gate 2A - Topology scalar:** current topology can be selected through existing Neighbor operators and reduced into a topology-derived scalar.
  312: - **Gate 2B - Composition:** base and topology scalars combine through a supplied composition policy without hard-coding mathematics into the emitter.
  313: - **Gate 3 - Complete resolved emission:** consumer value, current topology, scalar reduction, and composition resolve through one source-safe internal operation.
  314: - **Gate 4 - Resolved emission carrier:** exact emitter identity, arbitrary consumer vocabulary, finite resolved magnitude, and snapshot stability survive in an immutable carrier.
  315: - **Gate 5 - Propagation and vectors:** direct scalar propagation and arbitrary N-dimensional named-vector propagation preserve exact source/component/relationship provenance. Vector propagation requires normalization, keeps extreme resolved magnitudes, freezes the evaluated distance, and returns immutable carriers.
  316: - **Gate 6 - Eligibility:** scalar and vector eligibility evaluate the exact received propagated value. Eligible and ineligible facts remain present, ordering and dimensions remain authoritative, and decisions survive later topology changes without state mutation or consumer interpretation.
  317: 
  318: Gate 6 certification specifically proves:
  319: 
  320: - received value is the authoritative eligibility input;
  321: - exact-threshold inclusion is preserved;
  322: - arbitrary `N` survives through eligibility;
  323: - zero, partial, and all-component eligibility are represented honestly;
  324: - vector dimensions and component ordering cannot be rewritten;
  325: - eligibility vectors snapshot caller-owned decision collections;
  326: - complete Gate 5 provenance survives into Gate 6;
  327: - scalar and vector decisions remain stable after live topology changes.
  328: 
  329: Emission certification reports are written under:
  330: 
  331: ```text
  332: Certification/
  333: `-- Reports/
  334:     `-- Emission/
  335:         |-- emitter-certification-<timestamp>.log
  336:         `-- emitter-certification-latest.log
  337: ```
  338: 
  339: The next boundary is Gate 7: translate an eligible propagated fact into an immutable generic state operation against the exact consumer-owned target. Gate 7 must preserve target identity, arbitrary state vocabulary, value provenance, and explicit add/update/remove semantics without performing consumer interpretation inside Wilds Core.
  340: 
  341: ## Proposed Timeline routing
  342: 
  343: Timeline routing follows Neighbor membership because membership may participate in determining whether a resulting Moment continues the active semantic stream.
  344: 
  345: A Timeline represents one contiguous run of Moments belonging to the same semantic state or processing domain.
  346: 
  347: This routing policy remains proposed behavior.
  348: 
  349: ### Proposed Neighbor-driven Pulse propagation
  350: 
  351: Established Neighbor topology, propagation, eligibility, and emission resolution provide the foundation for a causal boundary between independently executing Wilds objects.
  352: 
  353: An eligible Neighbor does not become additional work owned by the originating Pulse. The intended model allows that Neighbor to receive a causal stimulus and independently originate a new Pulse.
  354: 
  355: **Causal provenance connects execution without merging execution ownership.**
  356: 
  357: Causal stimulus delivery and independent Neighbor Pulse creation remain proposed behavior and will be certified only after the resolved-emission handoff and receiver state boundary are stable.
  358: 
  359: ## Consumer-facing API direction
  360: 
  361: The exposed boundary is clear even though the final convenience API can continue to evolve:
  362: 
  363: - **Wilds is the front door.**
  364: - consumers provide their objects, vocabulary, state, and rules to Wilds;
  365: - Wilds owns Pulse/WorkUnit creation and lifecycle resolution;
  366: - Wilds owns relationships and emission-resolution mechanics;
  367: - QSL-backed computation is delegated behind the Wilds boundary;
  368: - WildsQslExecutor is integration machinery and should not be treated as the intended consumer construction/invocation surface;
  369: - WildsQslRequest is the certified integration envelope carrying source, consumer bindings, and attached state;
  370: - propagation is a Wilds policy and does not gate whether QSL can process valid delegated work;
  371: - QSL's result returns to Wilds, where the terminal Moment and history are resolved.
  372: 
  373: Consumer vocabulary remains consumer-owned. Wilds coordinates it; QSL computes against the runtime context it is given.
  374: 
  375: ## Milestones
  376: 
  377: ### Milestone 1: Neighbor topology and relationships
  378: 
  379: **CERTIFIED**
  380: 
  381: Membership participates in relationship identity; distance is mutable relationship state; duplicate relationships are rejected; relationships are directional; the same Neighbor may participate through multiple memberships; and topology operators are deterministic and source-safe.
  382: 
  383: ### Milestone 2: Neighbor propagation and eligibility mechanics
  384: 
  385: **CERTIFIED**
  386: 
  387: Exponential attenuation, zero-distance and zero-decay behavior, inclusive minimum-intensity eligibility, invalid-input rejection, and topology-to-propagation-to-eligibility composition are certified.
  388: 
  389: ### Milestone 3: Emission resolution
  390: 
  391: **CERTIFIED THROUGH GATE 3**
  392: 
  393: Consumer-owned values, current Neighbor topology, topology scalar reduction, and supplied composition resolve into one authoritative source-safe emission scalar.
  394: 
  395: ### Milestone 4: Resolved emission carrier
  396: 
  397: **CERTIFIED**
  398: 
  399: The immutable carrier preserves exact source identity, arbitrary consumer emission identity, finite resolved magnitude, and snapshot stability without owning propagation behavior.
  400: 
  401: ### Milestone 5: Resolved emission propagation and vector carriers
  402: 
  403: **CERTIFIED**
  404: 
  405: Direct scalar propagation and arbitrary N-dimensional vector propagation preserve resolved, normalized, and received values. Vector grouping, normalization, dimension/order invariants, exact relationship identity, frozen propagation distance, and collection immutability are certified.
  406: 
  407: ### Milestone 6: Receiver eligibility
  408: 
  409: **CERTIFIED**
  410: 
  411: Eligibility evaluates received propagated values, retains eligible and ineligible facts, supports arbitrary N-dimensional vectors, preserves exact provenance, exposes descriptive count/any/all summaries, and remains historically stable after live topology changes. No receiver mutation or consumer interpretation occurs.
  412: 
  413: ### Milestone 7: Receiver state boundary
  414: 
  415: **NEXT**
  416: 
  417: Translate an eligible propagated fact into a generic immutable state operation against the exact consumer-owned target.
  418: 
  419: Target behaviors:
  420: 
  421: - exact receiver/target identity survives;
  422: - arbitrary state vocabulary survives;
  423: - source eligibility and propagated provenance remain reachable;
  424: - state add, update, set, or remove semantics are explicit rather than inferred;
  425: - operation creation does not immediately mutate consumer state;
  426: - Wilds remains independent of consumer-specific object types;
  427: - QSL is not required for the Core state-operation boundary.
  428: 
  429: ### Milestone 8: Wilds-facing end-to-end emission vertical slice
  430: 
  431: **PLANNED**
  432: 
  433: Certify one authoritative Wilds route from consumer-owned values and topology through resolution, immutable carriers, vector normalization, propagation, eligibility, and resolved state output. Topology may change between evaluations, unfamiliar consumer vocabulary remains valid, and Wilds remains the public coordination surface.
  434: 
  435: ### Milestone 9: QSL downstream integration and conformance
  436: 
  437: **PLANNED**
  438: 
  439: Where scripting is requested, hand already-valid Wilds state operations through the existing internal QSL integration boundary without making QSL the simulation authority. Preserve the QSL core baseline, request-envelope certification, provenance continuity, runtime isolation, exact consumer-object identity, and arbitrary runtime-attached vocabulary.
  440: 
  441: Future causal Neighbor execution, semantic Timeline routing, and final convenience API freezing remain follow-on milestones after the receiver state boundary and full emission vertical slice are stable.
  442: 
  443: **Wilds is the exposed surface and owns coordination, request lifecycle, relationships, emission resolution, propagation, eligibility, and history. QSL owns delegated computation. The consumer owns meaning.**

    1: # Wilds Gate 8 - Emitter Surface
    2: 
    3: Wilds-facing emission orchestration contract and acceptance criteria
    4: 
    5: Status: PROPOSED • Next implementation boundary
    6: 
    7: Gate 8 exists to expose the already-certified emission route through one Wilds-owned surface. It must make the emitter usable without making the emitter smarter.
    8: 
    9: ## 1. Purpose
   10: 
   11: Gates 1 through 7 certify the emission machinery from consumer-owned state through topology-aware resolution, propagation, eligibility, and consumer-supplied instruction resolution. Gate 8 does not redefine those mechanics. It coordinates them behind one Wilds-facing operation.
   12: 
   13: ```text
   14: consumer-owned participant
   15:         |
   16:         v
   17: Wilds-facing emission request
   18:         |
   19:         v
   20: certified Gates 1-7
   21:         |
   22:         v
   23: ordinary Wilds instruction output
   24:         |
   25:         v
   26: Wilds lifecycle and history
   27:         |
   28:         v
   29: STOP before instruction execution or consumer-state mutation
   30: ```
   31: 
   32: ## 2. Architectural terminology
   33: 
   34: A consumer-owned object is a participant in Wilds. Source and receiving roles describe positions in a particular interaction; they are not separate Wilds Core entity types.
   35: 
   36: - A participating consumer-owned object may expose state, emitter behavior, emission rules, topology, and processing behavior.
   37: 
   38: - The same object may participate as the contextual source of one interaction and on the receiving side of another.
   39: 
   40: - Gate 8 must not introduce IReceiver, Receiver, or a permanent source/receiver hierarchy.
   41: 
   42: - Wilds owns generic mechanics. The consumer owns domain objects, vocabulary, state, policies, and semantic meaning.
   43: 
   44: ## 3. Gate 8 non-goals
   45: 
   46: - No new emission mathematics.
   47: 
   48: - No new topology mechanics.
   49: 
   50: - No new propagation semantics.
   51: 
   52: - No new eligibility semantics.
   53: 
   54: - No new instruction semantics.
   55: 
   56: - No receiver abstraction.
   57: 
   58: - No emission-specific registry or processor architecture.
   59: 
   60: - No QSL dependency in Wilds Core.
   61: 
   62: - No implicit instruction execution.
   63: 
   64: - No implicit consumer-state mutation.
   65: 
   66: - No causal Neighbor chaining or semantic Timeline routing in this gate.
   67: 
   68: ## 4. Minimal surface
   69: 
   70: The target surface should be intentionally small: one request contract and one Wilds-facing operation. A new result wrapper should be added only if the existing Moment result cannot carry the Gate 7 output without losing information.
   71: 
   72: ### Conceptual request contract
   73: 
   74: ```text
   75: public interface IEmissionRequest
   76: {
   77:     IEmitter Emitter { get; }
   78: 
   79:     INeighborRelationship Relationship { get; }
   80: 
   81:     // Use the existing certified Gate 6 policy contract.
   82:     // Do not create a duplicate eligibility abstraction for Gate 8.
   83: 
   84:     IEmissionInstructionResolver InstructionResolver { get; }
   85: }
   86: ```
   87: 
   88: The exact Gate 6 policy property is intentionally left to repository alignment. Gate 8 must reuse the certified eligibility contract rather than inventing a second one.
   89: 
   90: ### Wilds-facing operation
   91: 
   92: ```text
   93: ValueTask<IMoment> EmitAsync(
   94:     IEmissionRequest request,
   95:     CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
   96: ```
   97: 
   98: The spelling and concrete return type should follow the existing WildsEngine public conventions. The architectural requirement is that the consumer invokes one Wilds-owned operation and receives the ordinary Wilds temporal result.
   99: 
  100: ### Result discipline
  101: 
  102: Prefer the existing Moment and its Result over a new IEmissionResult wrapper. If the Gate 7 output can be carried directly as the authoritative Moment result, Gate 8 should not wrap it merely to label it as emission output.
  103: 
  104: ```text
  105: Gate 8 request
  106:       |
  107:       v
  108: Wilds lifecycle
  109:       |
  110:       v
  111: Moment
  112:       |
  113:       +-- Outcome
  114:       +-- Result = ordinary Gate 7 output
  115:       +-- WorkUnitIds
  116:       `-- Exception when failed
  117: ```
  118: 
  119: ## 5. Slice 1 scope
  120: 
  121: Slice 1 certifies exactly one scalar interaction. Vector support remains certified internally and can be surfaced in a later Gate 8 slice without changing lifecycle ownership.
  122: 
  123: ```text
  124: one emitter
  125:     -> one named scalar emission
  126:     -> one exact Neighbor relationship
  127:     -> one propagated fact
  128:     -> one eligibility decision
  129:     -> zero or one ordinary Wilds instruction
  130:     -> one authoritative Wilds Moment
  131: ```
  132: 
  133: ## 6. Acceptance criteria
  134: 
  135: ### Surface
  136: 
  137: - [ ] A consumer can initiate a complete certified scalar emission interaction through one Wilds-facing operation.
  138: 
  139: - [ ] The consumer does not manually coordinate Gates 1 through 7.
  140: 
  141: - [ ] The API reuses existing certified contracts where those contracts already satisfy the requirement.
  142: 
  143: - [ ] Gate 8 introduces no receiver-specific Core abstraction.
  144: 
  145: - [ ] Participating objects remain ordinary consumer-owned Wilds participants.
  146: 
  147: - [ ] Contextual source and receiving roles do not become permanent classifications.
  148: 
  149: ### Gate composition
  150: 
  151: - [ ] Gate 8 coordinates Gates 1 through 7 without changing their semantics.
  152: 
  153: - [ ] No downstream stage recalculates or replaces an authoritative upstream value.
  154: 
  155: - [ ] Resolved magnitude remains Gate 3/4 authority.
  156: 
  157: - [ ] Propagated magnitude remains Gate 5 authority.
  158: 
  159: - [ ] Eligibility remains Gate 6 authority.
  160: 
  161: - [ ] Consumer interpretation remains Gate 7 authority.
  162: 
  163: - [ ] Gate 8 adds orchestration, not another interpretation layer.
  164: 
  165: ### Identity and provenance
  166: 
  167: - [ ] Exact emitter identity survives the complete operation.
  168: 
  169: - [ ] Exact participating consumer-owned object identities survive wherever represented by the certified route.
  170: 
  171: - [ ] Exact Neighbor relationship identity survives.
  172: 
  173: - [ ] Arbitrary consumer-owned emission vocabulary survives unchanged.
  174: 
  175: - [ ] Gate 4 resolved provenance remains reachable.
  176: 
  177: - [ ] Gate 5 propagation provenance remains reachable.
  178: 
  179: - [ ] Gate 6 exact eligibility provenance remains reachable.
  180: 
  181: - [ ] Gate 7 instructions retain the exact eligibility decision that caused their resolution.
  182: 
  183: ### Eligibility and instruction resolution
  184: 
  185: - [ ] An eligible scalar fact may resolve to one ordinary Wilds instruction.
  186: 
  187: - [ ] An ineligible scalar fact produces no instruction.
  188: 
  189: - [ ] Ineligibility is not treated as execution failure.
  190: 
  191: - [ ] Gate 8 does not execute an instruction merely because Gate 7 resolved it.
  192: 
  193: - [ ] Gate 8 performs no implicit consumer-state mutation.
  194: 
  195: ### Wilds lifecycle
  196: 
  197: - [ ] The interaction enters the existing Wilds request lifecycle.
  198: 
  199: - [ ] Wilds owns the Pulse and required WorkUnit work.
  200: 
  201: - [ ] Successful orchestration produces one authoritative completed Moment.
  202: 
  203: - [ ] Failure produces an honest failed Moment rather than false success.
  204: 
  205: - [ ] Cancellation produces honest cancellation rather than false success.
  206: 
  207: - [ ] The terminal Moment enters Timeline exactly once.
  208: 
  209: - [ ] Timeline remains represented through Epoch according to the existing temporal model.
  210: 
  211: - [ ] No emission-specific temporal infrastructure is introduced.
  212: 
  213: ### Historical stability
  214: 
  215: - [ ] Changing live topology after a completed interaction does not rewrite recorded facts from that interaction.
  216: 
  217: - [ ] A later Gate 8 request observes the new topology.
  218: 
  219: - [ ] The earlier request continues to expose its original relationship, propagation, eligibility, and instruction provenance.
  220: 
  221: - [ ] Different requests represent distinct historical evaluations rather than mutable views of current topology.
  222: 
  223: ### Consumer neutrality
  224: 
  225: - [ ] Gate 8 accepts unfamiliar consumer-defined vocabulary.
  226: 
  227: - [ ] Gate 8 requires no game-specific Core types.
  228: 
  229: - [ ] A participating consumer-owned object may expose emitter behavior regardless of its role in another interaction.
  230: 
  231: - [ ] Gate 8 does not assume an emitting participant is permanently a source.
  232: 
  233: - [ ] Gate 8 does not assume another participant is permanently a receiver.
  234: 
  235: ### QSL boundary
  236: 
  237: - [ ] QSL is not required for a Core Gate 8 interaction.
  238: 
  239: - [ ] Gate 8 introduces no dependency from Wilds Core to QSL.
  240: 
  241: - [ ] Existing Wilds/QSL behavior remains unchanged.
  242: 
  243: - [ ] Scripted downstream computation remains outside Gate 8.
  244: 
  245: ### Regression gate
  246: 
  247: - [ ] Existing Gate 1 through 7 focused tests remain green.
  248: 
  249: - [ ] Gate 7 remains 12/12 unless deliberately extended with additional Gate 7 certification.
  250: 
  251: - [ ] Full Core Debug regression passes.
  252: 
  253: - [ ] Full Core Release regression passes.
  254: 
  255: - [ ] QSL core certification remains 156/156 with zero missing dependencies.
  256: 
  257: - [ ] Canonical Wilds/QSL consumer-state behavior remains Player.Health: 50 -> 41.3.
  258: 
  259: ## 7. Human certification story
  260: 
  261: Given a consumer-owned object with an emitter and another consumer-owned object related to it through Wilds topology, when the consumer invokes the Wilds-facing emission operation, Wilds coordinates the certified topology, propagation, eligibility, and instruction-resolution route, returns the resulting ordinary Wilds instruction through a completed Wilds lifecycle, and records the interaction in temporal history without executing the instruction or mutating consumer-owned state.
  262: 
  263: ```text
  264: Machine (consumer-owned)          Mara (consumer-owned)
  265:         |                                  |
  266:         | emitter                          | state / processors /
  267:         |                                  | possible own emitters
  268:         +---------- Neighbor --------------+
  269:                          |
  270:                          v
  271:                       Gate 8
  272:                          |
  273:                 coordinates Gates 1-7
  274:                          |
  275:                          v
  276:                ordinary IStateInstruction
  277:                          |
  278:                        STOP
  279: ```
  280: 
  281: ## 8. Implementation guardrail
  282: 
  283: Gate 8 should make the emitter usable, not make the emitter smarter.
  284: 
  285: If implementing Gate 8 requires substantial new evaluator logic, new emission mathematics, new receiver taxonomy, or new processing infrastructure, the implementation has likely crossed the boundary of the milestone. The preferred implementation is a thin composition layer over already-certified behavior.
  286: 
  287: ## 9. Pre-implementation repository alignment
  288: 
  289: - [ ] Crawl the current concrete Gates 1 through 7 API before freezing names.
  290: 
  291: - [ ] Map each request property to an existing certified abstraction.
  292: 
  293: - [ ] Confirm whether Moment.Result can carry the Gate 7 scalar output directly.
  294: 
  295: - [ ] Use existing WildsEngine execution conventions for cancellation, failure, Pulse, WorkUnit, Moment, Timeline, and Epoch.
  296: 
  297: - [ ] Create no abstraction solely because the surface document contains a conceptual slot for it.
  298: 
  299: ## 10. Definition of done
  300: 
  301: Gate 8 Slice 1 is complete when a consumer can call one Wilds-facing emission operation for one scalar interaction and Wilds owns the complete certified route through temporal history, while Gates 1 through 7 remain authoritative and unchanged.
  302: 
  303: The surface is successful when it feels boring: one clear entry point over machinery that already works.
